goal: Build a small React app this weekend, something like a habit tracker with local storage
interpretation: In a weekend, go from zero React to a working habit tracker (add, toggle and delete habits, persisted in localStorage) built with Vite and modern hooks.
assumptions: The habit tracker is a variation of the to-do and favorites apps in the videos: habits are items you add, toggle done and delete, with daily check-offs added on your own.
JavaScript with JSX is fine. Some videos use TypeScript, which you can ignore.
I could not see upload dates. I picked videos that show Vite and hooks, and left out the one flagged outdated_tooling.

sub_topics.title: Vite tooling and project structure
sub_topics.why: Replaces create-react-app. You need to scaffold, run and understand the project layout.

sub_topics.title: Components, JSX, props and useState
sub_topics.why: These are the core React mental model. State is what the habits list lives in.

sub_topics.title: Guided React project: lists, events, useEffect, context
sub_topics.why: Applies the basics in a full app with list rendering, conditional rendering and effects.

sub_topics.title: localStorage persistence and custom hooks
sub_topics.why: The key feature of the habit tracker. A reusable useLocalStorage hook is the idiomatic way to do it.

sub_topics.title: Build a CRUD tracker with local storage and a stats dashboard
sub_topics.why: A second, smaller build close to the habit tracker, with forms, a dashboard and persistence.

picks.title: Vite Crash Course – Frontend Build Tool
picks.reason: Covers Vite scaffolding, project structure, hot module replacement and production builds, which are the tooling gaps you named. The boilerplate it builds is a React app, so it gets you set up for the weekend.

evidence.quote: Vit is a next generation build tool that offers instant project startup and real-time updates
We learned how to build React apps with Vit, how to work with static assets, using environment variables, TypeScript

picks.confidence_note: It is a tooling crash course rather than a project, but it is the only substantial Vite coverage I found.

picks.title: Learn React Hooks: useState - Simply Explained!
picks.reason: A short, focused explanation of useState (state as data that changes over time, destructuring, setters in event handlers). It prepares you for the project builds.

evidence.quote: state the simplest way that you can think about this is data that changes with time
useState is the hook that you use in React to manipulate state
setCount and we're using this function to manipulate the state

picks.confidence_note: Concept explainer, but short and beginner-level, and it feeds straight into the projects.

picks.title: Learn React With This ONE Project
picks.reason: A project build that teaches components, JSX, useState, useEffect, lists, conditional rendering, context and localStorage-backed favorites. The favorites add/remove logic maps closely onto habit management.

evidence.quote: Everything revolves around something called a component. Now a component is really just a part of your application
JSX simply means kind of a combination of JavaScript and HTML. And you'll see that we have some things that look like HTML
When a state change occurs, the entire component is reran or rerendered. So if we just define something as a normal variable
A context will allow state to be globally available to anything that's within the provided context

picks.confidence_note: The movie API part is not needed for your app, but the rest is directly relevant.

picks.title: React Custom Hooks: useLocalStorage - Simply Explained!
picks.reason: Builds a reusable useLocalStorage custom hook with JSON serialization and try/catch. This is the component pattern to use for habit persistence.

evidence.quote: we are going to create a hook called use local storage that is going to expose to us three different functions
window local storage set item we're going to give it the key that we have here and then we're going to do json stringify
any component that wants to make use of the local storage can just use this hook directly and get access to all of these functions

picks.confidence_note: Uses TypeScript typing, which is a small hurdle. It is the second Cosden video, within the two-per-creator limit.

picks.title: Build a Complete To-Do List App with React + Vite | Dashboard, Reminders & Local Storage Tutorial
picks.reason: A Vite + React to-do build with add, edit and delete, a stats dashboard and local storage. It is the closest match to the habit tracker and works as a template for your own build.

evidence.quote: we are going to build a to-do list app using React plus white
we have a dashboard for showing our total task completed task pending task and overdue
use local storage so I'll copy this and I'll paste this
you can see the things are getting added and once you click on this it is incomplete

picks.confidence_note: Short and fast-paced. It uses Tailwind, which is extra to learn but optional.

warnings: Only about 185 of the 360 minutes are used. The remaining time is for building your own habit tracker, which is the real test. I did not pad with weak or redundant videos.
No video builds an actual habit tracker. The to-do and favorites builds are the closest, and you will need to add the daily check-off and streak logic yourself.
